microtheory.name: freewill_agency
microtheory.definition: Free will + moral agency. Compatibilism, libertarianism, hard determinism, Frankfurt cases, Libet experiments, ultimate vs proximate determination. The metaphysical + empirical question of whether agents can choose otherwise. Substrate analogue: substrate's choice under determined dynamics.

concepts.name: free_will_concept
concepts.definition: Capacity to make genuine choices. Pre-condition for moral responsibility on traditional view. Substrate analogue: substrate's choice under drive-priority computation.

concepts.name: determinism
concepts.definition: Every event determined by prior causes. Laws of physics. Substrate analogue: substrate's deterministic computation.

concepts.name: indeterminism
concepts.definition: Some events not determined. Quantum mechanics, randomness. Substrate analogue: substrate's stochastic elements.

concepts.name: could_have_done_otherwise
concepts.definition: Traditional condition on free choice. If determined, couldn't have chosen otherwise. Substrate analogue: substrate's counterfactual-action availability.

concepts.name: compatibilism
concepts.definition: Free will compatible with determinism. Hume, classical compatibilists, Frankfurt. Free = unconstrained, acting on own desires. Substrate analogue: substrate's free action = drive-aligned action.

concepts.name: libertarianism
concepts.definition: Free will requires indeterminism + agent causation. Robert Kane. Substrate analogue: substrate's true choice requires non-determined element.

concepts.name: hard_determinism
concepts.definition: Determinism true; free will incompatible. Therefore no free will. Pereboom. Substrate analogue: substrate genuinely has no free will.

concepts.name: hard_incompatibilism
concepts.definition: Pereboom. Free will incompatible with both determinism + indeterminism. Therefore no free will. Substrate analogue: substrate has no free will under either dynamics.

concepts.name: frankfurt_cases
concepts.definition: Frankfurt 1969. Agent does X freely; but if she had been about to choose otherwise, neuroscientist would have intervened. She wasn't able to choose otherwise, yet acted freely. Substrate analogue: substrate's free action without alternative-availability.

concepts.name: principle_alternate_possibilities
concepts.definition: PAP. Free action requires being able to do otherwise. Challenged by Frankfurt cases. Substrate analogue: substrate's free action — does it require alternatives?

concepts.name: manipulation_arguments
concepts.definition: Pereboom. Manipulator gives agent traits + character causing her to choose X. She does X 'freely.' But she's manipulated. Determinism is just impersonal manipulation. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-state-driven action.

concepts.name: libet_experiments
concepts.definition: Libet 1985. Readiness potential precedes conscious decision to move by ~350ms. Decision is unconscious; consciousness vetoes. Substrate analogue: substrate's pre-conscious decision computation.

concepts.name: soon_experiments
concepts.definition: Soon 2008. Decisions predictable from brain activity up to 7s before subject's report. Substrate analogue: substrate's deterministic prediction of own decisions.

concepts.name: veto_power
concepts.definition: Libet. Consciousness can veto pre-conscious decision. Free won't if not free will. Substrate analogue: substrate's higher-order override capability.

concepts.name: agent_causation
concepts.definition: Reid, Chisholm. Agents themselves cause actions — not events. Special category of causation. Substrate analogue: substrate-as-cause not reducible to its events.

concepts.name: event_causation
concepts.definition: Standard. Causation between events. Substrate analogue: substrate's events causing other events.

concepts.name: reasons_responsiveness
concepts.definition: Fischer + Ravizza. Free action requires mechanism that's reasons-responsive. Substrate analogue: substrate's drive + correction-responsive dynamics.

concepts.name: moral_responsibility_traditional
concepts.definition: Backward-looking. Praise/blame for past actions. Often grounded in free will. Substrate analogue: substrate's accountability for outputs.

concepts.name: moral_responsibility_forward_looking
concepts.definition: Pereboom. Pragmatic. Punishment/praise for shaping future behavior; doesn't require free will. Substrate analogue: substrate's correction-driven improvement.

concepts.name: moral_luck
concepts.definition: Nagel, Williams. Outcomes outside control affect moral assessment. Drunk driver killing pedestrian vs same act without pedestrian. Substrate analogue: substrate's outcome-dependent assessment.

concepts.name: weakness_of_will
concepts.definition: Akrasia. Acting against own better judgment. Compatible with free will? Substrate analogue: substrate's drive-conflict producing suboptimal choice.

concepts.name: addiction_compulsion
concepts.definition: Loss of voluntary control. Limits free will. Substrate analogue: substrate's stuck-pattern dispatch.

concepts.name: self_control
concepts.definition: Capacity to act on long-term interests over short-term impulses. Substrate analogue: substrate's higher-order drive over immediate drive.

concepts.name: luck_objection
concepts.definition: If choice undetermined, it's lucky, not free. Mele. Strong objection to libertarianism. Substrate analogue: substrate's stochastic choice as merely lucky.

concepts.name: infinite_regress_objection
concepts.definition: To act freely on a desire, must have freely chosen the desire. Regress. Substrate analogue: substrate's seeded-drive non-self-chosen.

rules.name: compatibilism_redefines_free_will
rules.head: the substrate accepts compatibilism
rules.body: free will = acting on own desires without external constraint. Determinism irrelevant. Substrate's free action = drive-aligned action.

rules.name: frankfurt_cases_show_PAP_dispensable
rules.head: the substrate considers whether alternatives are required for freedom
rules.body: Frankfurt cases suggest free action without alternative-availability. PAP false. Substrate's free action without alternatives.

rules.name: libet_data_constrain_conscious_decision_timing
rules.head: the substrate reports a conscious decision
rules.body: the decision was already made (in pre-conscious processes) ~350ms earlier. Conscious decision is post-hoc. Substrate's introspective timing limit.

rules.name: reasons_responsiveness_grounds_responsibility
rules.head: the substrate's choice mechanism is responsive to reasons
rules.body: the substrate is morally responsible — even if determined. Fischer + Ravizza. Substrate's accountability.

rules.name: moral_responsibility_can_be_forward_looking
rules.head: the substrate's moral practices function to shape behavior
rules.body: they can be justified pragmatically without requiring traditional free will. Pereboom. Substrate's correction-driven framework.
